Cut the sphere with two parallel planes a distance \(d\) from the centre (so the planes are at \(z=\pm d\)).

\[

---

### Volume of a spherical cap  

A cap of height \(h\) on a sphere of radius \(R\) has volume  

\[
V_{\text{cap}}=\frac{\pi h^{2}(3R-h)}{3}.
\]

Hence the two caps together have volume  

\[
2V_{\text{cap}}= \frac{2\pi h^{2}(3R-h)}{3}.
\]

---

### Remaining volume (the bowl’s interior)

The whole sphere has volume \(\displaystyle V_{\text{sphere}}=\frac{4\pi R^{3}}{3}\).  
The interior of the bowl (the part left after the caps are removed) is  

\[
V=V_{\text{sphere}}-2V_{\text{cap}}
   =\frac{4\pi R^{3}}{3}-\frac{2\pi h^{2}(3R-h)}{3}.
\]

We are told that this should be \(\frac{13}{27}\) of the sphere’s volume:

\[
\frac{4\pi R^{3}}{3}-\frac{2\pi h^{2}(3R-h)}{3}
      =\frac{13}{27}\cdot\frac{4\pi R^{3}}{3}.
\]

Cancel \(\pi/3\) and simplify:

\[
4R^{3}-2h^{2}(3R-h)=\frac{13}{27}\cdot4R^{3},
\qquad
2h^{2}(3R-h)=\frac{14}{27}\,4R^{3}.
\]

Thus

\[
h^{2}(3R-h)=\frac{28}{27}R^{3}.
\]

Let \(x=\dfrac{h}{R}\) (\(0\le x\le1\)). Then

\[
x^{2}(3-x)=\frac{28}{27}.
\]

This cubic simplifies to  

\[
27x^{3}-81x^{2}+28=0
\;\Longrightarrow\; (3x-2)(9x^{2}-21x-14)=0.
\]

The only admissible root in \([0,1]\) is  

\[
3x-2=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=\frac{2}{3}.
\]

Hence  

\[
h=\frac{2}{3}R,\qquad d=R-h=R-\frac{2}{3}R=\frac13R .
\]

---

\[
\boxed{\dfrac13}
\]

So the cuts should be made at a distance equal to one‑third of the sphere’s radius from the centre.<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
